headline: Gartner predicts that more than half of today's quantum computing startups will be out of business by 2030.
score_reason: Forecast from a major analyst firm; a prediction, not an event, and the original Gartner note was not read.
importance_line: Investors, staff and customers of small quantum firms face a possible shakeout according to one analyst's forecast, which is a prediction and not a finding, and Gartner itself says early signs of practical business advantage are appearing.
summary: The Register reports, citing analyst firm Gartner, that 200 to 300 quantum startups are chasing a market Gartner expects to bring in $1.1 billion worldwide in 2027, up from $869.9 million forecast this year, and that customers will reject firms that fail to deliver fault-tolerant machines (computers that stay reliable despite hardware errors). Gartner expects the public sector to spend most at first, with banking, finance and insurance overtaking it in 2028.
notes: Read in full at The Register; Gartner's own report not opened.
